| File | Change |

| `apps/web/src/styles/dialogs.css` | `.artifact-modal-panel` → `width: min(1600px, calc(100vw - 80px))`, `height: min(960px, calc(100vh - 80px))`. `.artifact-modal-body` gets `flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0` (it owns the leftover height and the scroll), header and mode tabs are pinned with `flex: 0 0 auto`. Smaller windows behave as before: 1280×800 → panel 1200×633 with the same fill (body 491px, bottom 1px above the panel edge); `<=900px` still goes full screen.

411.body:
Local source startup can send adapter HTTP/WebSocket calls and curl health checks through an inherited outbound proxy when `NO_PROXY` is missing or contains `127.*`, which is not interpreted consistently across clients. Keep loopback service traffic direct without requiring users to repair their shell proxy configuration.

Fixes #296.

The proxy-routing failure was reproduced locally. This addresses a plausible cause of the reported `legacy_unavailable` / `PoolTimeout`; it does not establish that every timeout in the issue has the same cause.

## Loopback transport and startup probes

- Add a shared adapter helper to recognize localhost and loopback IP addresses. HTTPX mounts bypass proxies for local service targets while retaining environment proxy selection and TLS certificate settings for remote targets.
- Disable automatic proxy selection for local gateway WebSocket connections on versions that support it; retain compatibility with older websockets releases and remote gateway behavior.
- Make source-stack health probes explicitly bypass loopback addresses while retaining existing bypass exclusions. The JiuwenSwarm test wrapper probes its fixed loopback target directly.
- Document the transport policy and add regression cases covering IPv4, IPv6, localhost, remote proxy use, proxy-free operation, HTTP/SOCKS proxy environments, and older WebSocket clients.

There is overlap with the adapter transport work in open PR #285; maintainers should coordinate the two before merging.

## Conflict resolution and current validation

Rebased onto upstream main `e7d559282035d78932c5a159f6dab620dcbf18c3`; the PR contains exactly one commit, `0ae03149e5035fb0fe6021edbd2e771233ea18e3`.

The conflict in adapter client initialization is resolved by retaining upstream's `httpx[socks]` dependency and separate model client/router. All three HTTP clients apply loopback-only direct mounts while retaining environment proxy selection and CA settings. Remote model requests continue to use the dedicated model client and their configured outbound proxy. The upstream constructor-argument assertion is replaced with a startup/health regression under a SOCKS environment, and real loopback HTTP tests now cover SOCKS and the dedicated model client.

Verified on the new commit under WSL2:
- Adapter non-live suite: **272 passed, 0 failed**, 12 marker warnings; includes **32 network cases**. Command: `cd services/adapter && uv run --locked --extra test pytest --ignore=tests/test_gateway_live.py --ignore=tests/test_real_llm.py -q`.
- `bash -n scripts/start-stack.sh scripts/with-jiuwenswarm.sh`: passed.
- `git diff --check e7d55928 HEAD`: passed.
- Full UT/ST/browser E2E layers were not rerun for this conflict update. The previously documented gateway/configuration blockers below remain unresolved; those historical results do not validate the new SHA. This update does not certify the complete local-stack journey.
- [Current CI run 39359166726](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/39359166726): policy selection and L1 static checks passed. UT, ST, mocked E2E, Coverage and merge-gate were skipped under the draft policy; this is not a full CI gate pass.

## Historical validation before rebase

Tested commit: `1ebb37c15ef0bd4d2ec215cee9f84c438661013e` (Linux/amd64 under WSL2).

- Adapter non-live suite: **268 passed, 0 failed**, 12 marker warnings. Command: `cd services/adapter && uv run --extra test pytest --ignore=tests/test_gateway_live.py --ignore=tests/test_real_llm.py -q`. Includes 29 network regression cases exercising both proxy-free and inherited broken-proxy configurations.

- UT: wrapper exits 2 before test collection because `/agent/info` reports the JiuwenSwarm gateway unreachable (WebSocket opening handshake timeout). No frozen UT plan or executed-test accounting was produced. The same command on unmodified upstream main `a0cf9c77c43ae046da078a398a9abc4420cf68b1` exits 2 before collection with the same handshake timeout. This host blocker reproduces without the patch; no UT cases executed in either run.
- ST: **15 planned / 15 executed / 14 passed / 1 failed / 0 skipped**, from the frozen-plan summary. The failed identity is `check:swarm-sdk-contract`; its nested pytest report contains 69 cases, 26 failures and 1 error, including outbound-bridge timeouts. A baseline ST attempt was stopped during preparation; attribution of this failure remains unresolved. No assertions were weakened.
- Browser E2E: **89 planned**; the completed research batch reports **20 executed / 0 passed / 20 failed / 0 skipped**, with HTTP 401 during model/quota setup. The remaining batches were stopped after identifying the local configuration conflict; there is no complete layer summary. Local `.env` overrides conflict with the isolated stack's port/authentication settings. A baseline browser attempt was stopped during preparation, so baseline attribution remains incomplete. These results are not claimed as proxy-regression evidence.

GitHub Actions readback: [CI run 39254149347](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/39254149347) passed policy selection and L1 static checks. UT, ST, mocked E2E, Coverage and merge-gate were skipped under the draft policy; this is not a full CI pass.

412.author: zy95-12
412.body:
Explicit delegated tasks can now use Codex as a Specialist runtime while keeping ScienceDiscovery's child Workspace, Brief, execution permissions, timeline and Artifact publication paths. Missing credentials pause the child and show an in-conversation API-key config card, backed by the platform encrypted secret channel.

Refs #385. This is only the locked 2026-10-19 MVP; it does not close the full issue.

## Behavior and compatibility

- Specialist create/update/read accepts credential-free `runtime: {kind: "codex", model?: string}`. Omitted or native runtime keeps existing behavior and the exact legacy configuration hash; only non-native runtime enters the hash.
- Explicit `task(specialistId=…)` replaces the child's model-loop factory with the pinned official Codex SDK. Structured Codex decisions request validated platform tools; its native shell is disabled, its sandbox is read-only, and it runs in fresh private scratch/HOME directories. Product commands still use platform execution bindings, never a Codex host shell.
- Normalized started/progress/tool_call/file_change/need_input/done events map to existing child timeline/results, including usage and Codex thread ID. Artifacts come only from platform declaration receipts.
- Config credentials never enter Specialist metadata, argv, model prompts or chat. The dedicated authenticated endpoint stores a Session-scoped encrypted key; Session/Project deletion removes it. Always-allow does not supply credentials. Codex children use platform permission decisions even when their lead uses JiuwenSwarm.

## Validation

Candidate: `88a936f7`.

- Focused runtime UT/ST: **21 passed, 0 failed/skipped** (20 UT + 1 ST). Includes official SDK transport with a synthetic executable, real pinned SDK/CLI against a loopback Responses fixture, platform execution/Artifact handoff, event mapping, invalid decisions/arguments, cancellation/deadline, encrypted-secret/reload/hash behavior, mixed Swarm/Codex permission routing and preservation of the frozen Brief/platform history on continuation. No vendor/model traffic.
- Adjacent regression: **115 passed, 0 failed/skipped** across Store, built-in specialists, Subagent lifecycle, AgentRun and Idea Tree composition.
- Full workspace + test TypeScript checks passed; API/test checks repeated after the permission fix.
- L1: **4 planned / 4 executed / 4 passed**, including architecture, docs, catalog and E2E metadata.
- Broader ST: initially **17 planned / 17 executed / 16 passed / 1 failed**. The failure is `check:swarm-sdk-contract` → `test_100_concurrent_calls_keep_identity_and_execute_once` (3-second timeout). The changed branch has no changes to those Python tests, adapter sources or Swarm patches. Unmodified main passed **16/16** planned ST checks; its standalone Python contract passed **66 tests + 3 subtests**. An isolated candidate rerun at `9f96171d` passed **17/17**, with no intervening product changes. The initial timeout remains disclosed; its exact cause was not established. The final follow-up only preserves continuation context in the adapter and is covered by the 21 focused checks.
- Full UT was interrupted by the host reboot and has no final verdict. Focused checks above were rerun afterward; the complete UT and mocked-browser suites are not claimed.

Node UT/ST coverage of new executable runtime modules: **99% lines / 95.20% branches / 87.50% functions** (`agent`, `codex`, `config`, `permissions`; the contract file is types only). Node/tsx reports the closing sink block in `agent.ts` as uncovered (lines 36–37); done-event behavior is asserted. Remaining branches/functions include optional compatibility/default-factory paths and defensive error handling. These measurements do not quantify all added lines in the existing Store/HTTP/run/UI files; those have targeted regression/browser evidence rather than a full added-line coverage claim. Real CLI cancellation after spawn/descendant shutdown and provider-auth success are not established by the synthetic stream cancellation checks.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS**, tested `88a936f7`: normal product startup with isolated data/ports, loopback-only scripted lead and public browser/API path. The focused journey registers a Codex specialist, explicitly delegates under Always-allow, observes the interactive password config card, checks input bounds at **390×900 and 1440×900 (DPR 1)**, cancels the child, and verifies stale secret submission returns 409.

- Native lead: **1 executed / 1 passed / 0 failed/skipped**.
- Default JiuwenSwarm lead: **1 executed / 1 passed / 0 failed/skipped**, plus **9/9** supplemental backend checks.
- Commands: `CI_E2E_BACKEND=legacy CI_E2E_GREP='Show Codex auth card' bash .ci/run-e2e.sh mocked`, and the same command with `CI_E2E_BACKEND=jiuwenswarm` (prepared dependencies and separate run-owned data/ports).

Successful card-to-vendor authentication/model completion was not exercised; secret acceptance and SDK/CLI completion are covered separately with synthetic credentials and a local provider. No paid provider validation is claimed.

## Later phases

Host-process confinement/hardening, durable Codex thread continuation and crash recovery, browser/device OAuth and broader credential management, ACP, additional SDKs, runtime picker/probe UI, #64, and full Skills/MCP bridging remain outside this PR. The adapter exposes a focused platform tool subset. Existing platform execution/artifact semantics are reused; this does not implement the earlier broad Runner/ACP prototypes.

## Release

Release category: release:feature

User impact: explicit Codex-backed Specialist delegation and an in-conversation credential card.

Compatibility and migration: none for existing native specialists and clients; new runtime metadata is opt-in.

421.author: zy95-12
421.body:
Refs #385.

Codex Specialist tasks now run the model transport inside the Runner's Bubblewrap/seccomp launch boundary, with inner Codex `danger-full-access`. Platform tools keep their own Runner execution and offline/allowlist network permissions. Explicit declarations are the only deliverable handoff: undeclared files do not create Artifacts, file-change steps, generated-file provenance, or execution Workspace snapshots/diffs.

**Dependency:** stacked on the still-open MVP #412. This PR targets `main` and currently includes the MVP commits. Resolve that dependency and rebase when appropriate; do not merge #412 as part of this work. This PR does not close #385 or implement Phase 3.

**Draft / DoD gap:** successful live Codex authentication is blocked by the absence of an approved API key. Do not merge until the remaining live-auth matrix is verified.

## Behavior

- Same-channel Specialist chat can apply validated model, reasoning, wall-clock timeout and fallback settings through `configure_specialist_runtime`. The existing secret card remains the configuration fallback and can disable native recovery before startup. Credentials stay outside chat, catalog metadata and argv.
- Each task has an independent Workspace and private `CODEX_HOME`. The pinned CLI uses the Runner launch implementation locally on the API host; native Codex shell/MCP/search/subagents are disabled or rejected, and project `.codex` configuration is masked. There is no shared sandbox. Linux/local Bubblewrap is required for the model-process sandbox.
- `declare_artifact(path|paths)` is the explicit handoff API; only successful platform receipts enter `artifacts[]`. Commands, execution status and logs remain auditable.
- Runtime startup/auth/tool unavailability defaults to a visible `builtin-code-engineer` fallback, with opt-out through profile/chat/card. Cancellation, deadlines, turn limits, ordinary task failures, denied direct consent and failures after potentially dispatched work do not replay work through fallback. Confirmed pre-dispatch tool blockers remain recoverable.
- Direct model execution requires explicit `runtime.execution=direct` plus separate `direct_code` consent. Tool direct execution uses the existing request/execute consent pair; sandbox Always Allow does not authorize it.

## Validation

- Focused UT: **169 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** across Specialist runtime, workspace bindings, shell observation, Runner lifecycle/sandbox/direct execution, CAS leases and provenance.
- Focused ST: **2 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**: official pinned Codex SDK/CLI through outer Bubblewrap + inner full access against a local Responses fixture; filesystem/environment/project-config isolation and nested-userns denial probe.
- L1: **planned 4 / executed 4 / passed 4**, no failures/skips.
- Type checks: test sources, API, Runner and web passed. Build passed; subsequent changes were rebuilt for affected packages.
- Browser: **1 passed, 0 failed/skipped; 4/4 journey steps**, password/config fallback and cancellation. Screenshots inspected at **390×900 and 1440×900**. The browser run used `d19dfc17`; later changes affect the launcher/docs/CLI driver, not the web bundle.
- Public API/production CLI journey: **5 scenarios passed**, plus startup (6/6 steps): explicit delegation/configuration and advanced settings/handoff, cancellation, timeout, fallback enabled, fallback disabled.
- Live invalid-key invocation: **2 scenarios passed**, plus startup (3/3 steps), using the actual pinned CLI/started Codex threads and the default live provider endpoint. This run used `ce7503de`; the final cancellation-race check is covered by focused UT and the repeated local API matrix. This exercises recovery on/off with deliberately invalid credentials; it does **not** certify successful authentication or provider work.

Commands: `node --import tsx --test <focused suites>`, `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`, package typechecks/builds, `pnpm ci:l1`, `SPECIALIST_BROWSER=1 node test/api/specialist-runtime-journey.mjs`, and `SPECIALIST_REAL=1 SPECIALIST_CASES=fallback-on,fallback-off node test/api/specialist-runtime-journey.mjs`.

Full `pnpm ci:ut` was attempted but blocked **before discovery**: the local JiuwenSwarm checkout lacks patch target files (`agent_ws_server.py`, `call_timeout_patch.py`). The same setup failure was reproduced with detached upstream/main `a0cf9c77` and the same fixture. No full-UT test counts are claimed. Full ST and full browser layers were not completed; targeted suites were used. Swarm-backend execution, remote model-process placement, macOS, successful live authentication and the remaining live scenarios are unverified. GitCode CodeCheck is ignored.

## DoD matrix

| Required path | Deterministic product coverage | Real Codex-auth coverage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Explicit task | PASS: explicit Specialist ID, frozen hash, separate Workspace/thread | Invalid-key invocation exercised; successful auth/work BLOCKED |
| Config card / same channel | PASS: browser password/opt-out/cancel; API key submission; settings applied by Specialist | Invalid-key config submission exercised; valid-key continuation BLOCKED |
| Cancel / timeout | PASS: active CLI/provider wait cancelled; deadline terminal status; no fallback/replay | BLOCKED without approved valid key |
| Explicit handoff | PASS: declared result only; scratch output omitted; execution snapshots suppressed | BLOCKED without approved valid key |
| Fallback enabled / disabled | PASS: terminal native recovery versus surfaced failure | PASS: started live CLI/thread with deliberately invalid key, recovery on/off |
| Nested sandbox probe | PASS: outer isolation + inner full access; nested userns denied | Live invalid-key CLI launches through the same outer sandbox |

Run the full successful-auth matrix with `SPECIALIST_REAL=1 SPECIALIST_KEY_FILE=<private-file> SPECIALIST_MODEL=<model> node test/api/specialist-runtime-journey.mjs`. The key is submitted through the private config endpoint and never put in argv.

## Phase 3 residuals

Durable provider-thread continuation beyond a task, additional runtimes/ACP, shared sandboxes, remote model-process scheduling, full observability, and full Skills/MCP bridging remain deferred. No Phase 3 work was started. Host ChatGPT OAuth is not imported; this configuration surface supports API keys.

## Release

Release category: release:feature
User impact: sandboxed Codex delegation, explicit deliverable handoff and configurable runtime recovery.

427.author: zhaozhaozz
427.body:
Clicking a CSV in the workspace file tree handed the file to the browser through `window.open`, so a raw upload or an intermediate table the agent wrote showed up in a new tab as plain text or a download. The same data opened in the interactive table viewer (Plotly charts, display filters, column-type inference) only when it was reached through the Artifact catalog. Researchers could not sanity-check their own table in the place they had just dropped it.

Fixes #43

## Workspace CSV files open in the existing table viewer

`openWorkspacePath` in `apps/web/src/App.tsx` still reads the file once through the existing `GET /api/sessions/:id/file` endpoint. After that read it now has three branches instead of two:

- `.md` / `.markdown` → the Markdown reader (unchanged);
- a file the table viewer already understands → the same `CsvArtifactWindow` the Artifact modal uses, opened in place and lazy-loaded, from the bytes just read;
- everything else → the previous `window.open` hand-off (unchanged).

The routing predicate is `opensInCsvViewer(path, mediaType)` in `apps/web/src/csvArtifact.ts`. It decides by file name (`.csv`, case-insensitive) or a CSV media type only. Content is not sniffed, so a `.txt` or log that happens to contain commas keeps opening in a new tab. `.tsv` and `.json` are not routed to the viewer, because the viewer only parses comma-separated text (`.tsv` Artifacts use the server-side table preview, not this viewer). No new format is added.

Nothing on the Artifact side is read or written: no catalog lookup, no version, no provenance. The click works for a file that was never declared.

## One viewer, two kinds of source

`CsvArtifactWindow` and its inspector took a `ScientificArtifactVersion` plus provenance. They now take `source: CsvViewerSource`, which is either `{ kind: "artifact", version, provenance }` or `{ kind: "workspace", path, sessionId, size, openedAt, modifiedAt?, revisionId? }`. `csvSourceRecord` turns either into the table's source record. The artifact branch is field-for-field what the viewer built before.

For a workspace file the viewer shows only facts it has. The header badge and subtitle say "Workspace file" instead of `v<n>`. The source strip shows the workspace path instead of a version id and the "Input version pinned" badge. The inspector's Provenance tab lists path, size, file modified time (when known) and read time, without a SHA-256 or a "Recorded provenance" section. The footer says the workspace file stays unchanged. The Artifact modal still shows the version, the pinned badge, the source Artifact and the recorded provenance as before.

Saved chart layouts are keyed by the workspace revision the file list reports for the path (`WorkspaceFile.provenance.revisionId`). Reopening the same revision restores the layout. An edited file gets a new revision and opens on fresh default charts, the same way a new Artifact version does. Without a revision the key falls back to path plus modification time.

Rendered review turned up one layout problem, which is fixed in `styles.css`. A long path squeezed the size/rows/fields facts onto two lines at 1024 px, and 10 px monospace underscores were clipped at 1x pixel density. The path now takes the free space, gives it up first, and has an explicit line height.

## Validation

All on the pushed commit `8ebe5fa6` (base `d1cf7975`):

- `apps/web` unit tests: 975 passed, 0 failed. New tests cover the routing predicate (CSV in; TSV, JSON, Markdown, text and extensionless files out), both source records and their layout-key fallbacks, revision-scoped layout restore and reset, and the `openWorkspacePath` branch order with a single file read.
- `apps/web` typecheck: clean.
- UT layer (`pnpm ci:ut`): planned 4356, executed 4356, passed 4347, failed 9. All nine are in `services/launcher` (`serve.test.ts` ×4, `source-evolve.test.ts` ×5). They write CommonJS fixture servers into `$TMPDIR`; the local run used a `TMPDIR` inside the repository tree, where the root `package.json` (`"type": "module"`) makes Node load those fixtures as ESM (`require is not defined`). Rerunning both files with a `TMPDIR` outside the tree: 38/38 passed. This change touches neither the launcher nor anything it imports.
- ST layer (`pnpm ci:st`): planned 24, executed 24, passed 19, failed 5. All five are in `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/process-adapters.st.test.ts` (sandboxed Claude/ACP transports). The same five fail on this host on unmodified `d1cf7975` in a separate detached worktree, and the ST job of main's Actions run at `d1cf7975` is green, so they are host-specific and pre-existing.
- E2E layer (`pnpm ci:e2e`): planned 95, executed 95, passed 89, failed 6; the new journey passed inside the layer. The host was running two other E2E layers at the same time. Isolated rerun of the six: 5 passed (`journey-compact-process`, `journey-custom-mcp`, `journey-first-run`, `journey-idea-tree-fixture`, `journey-model-settings`). In the full layer a custom-MCP run that timed out under load left an active run behind, and the three global-isolation journeys after it then failed their stack reset with HTTP 409. `journey-model-connect-wizard` still fails on this host on a layout assertion (submit button bottom 601 px, expected < 580 px). It fails with the same numbers on a build of unmodified `d1cf7975`, and passes in main's Actions run at `d1cf7975`.

Visual check of the real build in Chromium at 1440×900 and 1024×700 (English), and at 820×768 and 390×844 (Chinese). It covered long nested paths, a CJK path, and the inspector Provenance tab, plus the Artifact modal opening the same viewer as a regression check. Nothing overflowed the page, and both panel toggles stayed reachable in every state. At 820 px and below the existing responsive layout hides the file heading and the source-strip facts, for Artifacts and workspace files alike. That behaviour is unchanged.

## E2E user journeys

New mocked browser journey `test/journey-workspace-csv-preview.spec.ts` — **PASS** (1/1, and 3/3 with `--repeat-each=3`) against an isolated local API + Runner with a journey-owned stub model, and inside the E2E layer above:

1. Upload `measurements.csv` and a comma-rich `run-notes.txt` through the workspace drop zone → both appear in the Workspace files tree.
2. Click the CSV in the tree → the table viewer opens in the page with the "Workspace file" badge. No tab opens. Exactly one `GET …/file?path=measurements.csv` is issued and no write request.
3. In the viewer → a chart renders, the encoding options list `expression / quantitative`, the category filter offers the missing `condition` value, and searching `S-03` leaves 1 visible record. Esc closes it.
4. The agent writes `scratch/undeclared.csv` with `run_shell` and does not declare it → the file is in the tree and not in the Artifact catalog.
5. Click the undeclared CSV → the same viewer opens it and shows its workspace path.
6. Click `run-notes.txt` → it still opens in a new browser tab (`blob:` URL), and no viewer appears.

Uploaded files are also registered as `uploaded` Artifacts by the existing upload flow, which is why step 4 uses an undeclared file to show that no declaration is needed.

## Release

Release category: release:feature
User impact: CSV files in the workspace file tree open in the interactive table viewer (charts, filters, column types) in place, without being declared as Artifacts. Other workspace files open as before.
Compatibility and migration: none. No API change. Chart layouts saved for Artifacts keep their keys.

On a large screen the artifact viewer was still a small card: `.artifact-modal-panel` was `width: min(1080px, 100%)` with only a max height, so on a 1920px window plots, tables, notebooks and source previews used about half of the screen. JiuwenSwarm's background Skill-index requests were counted as Session turns by both cancellation-test gateways. This produced false queue-ordering failures (`2 !== 1`) and could leave an active or blocked run hanging after an assertion failed. The fixtures now answer no-tools housekeeping requests without counting them, and both queue tests cancel remaining work in `finally`.

Refs #251. Partial fix; keep #251 open pending repository-wide validation follow-up. All issue-specific scenarios below pass; the broader gates are not fully green. The default `/llm/default` ownership issue remains outside this change.

Baseline: `0d31e155a206c23f6d6a0c9632e44f516b326bbe`.

| Scenario | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Both fixtures ignore background requests before and after a Session turn, including streamed requests | Both new regression cases fail with the original fixtures | 2/2 pass; tool-enabled turns are still counted |
| Cancelling queued work never admits its prompt to the Session | Vulnerable fixture counted all requests | Pass in the full cancellation file |
| A blocked run holds its queue despite Skill-index background work | Real baseline emitted a no-tools request followed by a 68-tools request; assertion failed `2 !== 1`, then required a 60-second external timeout | Pass with real Swarm |
| Assertion failure cleans up queued and active/blocked work | Baseline failure left the worker hanging | Injected assertion failures in both queue cases: all runs cancelled, complete TAP output, normal exit 1 for the two intentional failures; no guard timeout |
| Skill changes trigger incremental indexing without invalidating queue assertions | Reproduced background-call interference after a Skill change | Blocked-queue case passes after adding another Skill to an isolated instance |

The patch changes only `services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts`.

Earlier candidate `cf93212f` (before replacing dynamic regression registration with static declarations):

- E2E: 70 planned, 44 executed, 39 passed, 5 failed, 0 skipped; subsequent backend startup was blocked. Logs include Swarm filesystem-lock release errors. No complete passing E2E run exists, and these earlier results are not claimed as final-candidate validation.

441.body:
Researchers can now inspect and retrieve structured scientific data from five built-in database connectors, then download selected files through governed artifact jobs. GEO uses actual provider file listings and bounded sample metadata queries; AlphaFold DB adds retrieval of existing predictions and confidence files. The change also strengthens ChEMBL measurement filtering, ClinVar submission preservation and experimental PDB provenance.

Refs #420. **Partial fix; keep #420 open.** This is a draft because broad verification is not green and provider failure-path coverage remains incomplete.

## Scope

- GEO: discover real matrix/SOFT/supplementary files, validate download selection, preserve study/sample/platform metadata, paginate sample annotations and avoid bulk-query timeouts. Correct accession request parameters and GEO directory buckets.
- ChEMBL: validate measurement constraints and preserve units, relations, target/molecule/assay identifiers and assay confidence. Advance pagination over scanned provider rows even when local confidence filtering returns an empty page.
- ClinVar: retrieve versioned VCV/RCV records and preserve individual SCV assertions and conflicting classifications, without inventing a consensus. Reject oversized XML explicitly.
- RCSB PDB: preserve experimental-method/revision evidence and include it with structure download candidates.
- AlphaFold DB: add existing-prediction lookup by UniProt accession and governed model/confidence downloads, with explicit predicted status and model version. This does not run prediction software.
- Reuse the existing Inspector for built-in sources, using the same broker/audit path; preserve AlphaFold selections across store reloads, refresh changed connector caches, register evidence graph tools and document all five sources in English and Chinese.

## Reproduction and acceptance evidence

Baseline: `0d31e155a206c23f6d6a0c9632e44f516b326bbe` (GitHub history). Product-validation candidate: `42a96f3f2613d34487ecc6041c61b5854b692d4c`. PR head: `bcd56b74bd9b79564e392da33e4977d94dd65034`. The final commit only relocates the unchanged connector-persistence test to avoid an append-at-end conflict with current main; production code and other tests are identical to the product-validation candidate.
The requester explicitly waived baseline reproduction for this feature. The baseline capability/gap assessment was source inspection, not a baseline live-service result. The candidate journeys below used built production API/Runner entry points, the bundled stdio MCP server, isolated Session/data state and official live providers. Agent validation used the native executor and a deterministic local model stub; it does not certify JiuwenSwarm or real-model behavior.

| Acceptance area | Candidate evidence | Status / remaining limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Five sources discoverable, enabled and callable | Production sources API, saved Session selections, five live Inspector calls; browser Inspector journey | PASS for representative paths; Agent tool execution exercised with AlphaFold, not every source |
| GEO metadata/files/verified matrix | GSE1000, sample annotations and actual directory listing; completed matrix download, SHA-256 and parsed 22,283 probe rows × 10 samples | PASS; identify expression profiling by array and avoid assuming raw counts |
| ChEMBL constrained measurements/pagination | CHEMBL203 activity query, two distinct provider pages, units/relations/assay metadata/confidence retained | PASS for representative query |
| ClinVar individual assertions/conflicts | Versioned VCV000014206 live lookup with distinct SCV submissions; structured XML/conflict fixtures | PASS for selected live record and fixture contracts; not an exhaustive clinical interpretation |
| Experimental structure and downstream reading | 1CRN completed download and checksum, parsed 327 atoms in chain A | PASS |
| Existing prediction/model/confidence | P69905 model CIF and confidence download, checksums, predicted marker/version, 142 pLDDT values | PASS |
| Evidence retained after analysis | Actual files read and analysis output persisted with source IDs/URLs/retrieval metadata | PASS in native product journey |
| Invalid/missing inputs and provider/download failures | Gateway/domain boundary tests, broker/artifact tests; invalid Inspector accession rejected and next turn usable | PARTIAL: full representative rate-limit/download-failure and all-backend coverage not established |
| Setup, supported operations and scientific limits | English/Chinese guides and reproducible examples; L1 documentation check | PASS |

## Validation

Previously executed local checks at the product-validation candidate are reported below; no unexecuted check is counted as passing. At the final PR head, the relocated persistence test was rerun (1 passed), L1 was rerun (4 planned / 4 executed / 4 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped), and `git diff --check` passed. A three-way merge-tree check against upstream main `9191d552d649612a81ec5852638020bcc1f30b7e` completed without conflicts; the merge result has not been executed. The earlier broad and product journey results remain attributed to their original tested SHA.

- Gateway Python suite: **38 passed** (includes 10 new domain tests).
- MCP sources tests: **30 passed**.

- Artifact manager tests: **2 passed**. AlphaFold selection persistence test: **1 passed**.

SDK contract suite failed: 33 passed / 33 failed out of 66, with test-server startup reporting `self.server.started == False`. The exact failing `TransportTests::test_concurrent_results_remain_correlated` was rerun on both the pristine baseline and candidate with the same SDK interpreter and failed identically (1 failed each). This establishes that representative startup failure on the baseline; it does not independently attribute every SDK failure.

Large valid numerical CSVs can fail to open because numeric profiling expands every value into `Math.min` / `Math.max` arguments and exceeds the JavaScript engine's argument limit. This fixes that failure and adds an explicit limit of **1,000,000 data records** to the CSV Visualization Workspace.

Fixes #446

## Changes

- Calculate numeric column extrema and bubble-size extrema iteratively, preserving the existing results without depending on the function-argument limit.
- Parse CSV records incrementally and abort when record 1,000,001 is encountered, before profiling or constructing a partial table. Headers and skipped blank records do not count; quoted newlines remain part of their CSV record.
- Accept exactly 1,000,000 data records. Above the limit, show English/Chinese guidance to process locally or split/sample the file. Do not silently truncate scientific data.
- Add regression tests for large numeric columns, the exact boundary, blank records, quoted newlines, chart scaling, and a browser upload/open/rejection/recovery journey.

The limit applies to opening CSVs in this viewer. It is not a server upload-size limit or a guarantee of bounded memory for very wide CSVs: supported content is still held and profiled in browser memory. Byte/column limits and worker-based processing are outside this first fix.

450.author: zhaozhaozz
450.body:
`pnpm ci:ut` ran the whole UT slice inside `scripts/with-jiuwenswarm.sh`, which exported `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXECUTOR=jiuwenswarm` and the shared adapter URL to every process of the run. Any test that booted `createApiServer` therefore pushed its settings to the one shared adapter, and the scheduler kept that safe by putting every file under `services/api/` on one lock, so the API files ran one after another while the default pool was two workers. Only two files actually start a gateway turn. This change makes unit tests start independently and run in parallel, and gives the one JiuwenSwarm instance only to the tests that declare they need it, one at a time.

Fixes #444

## A test declares the instance; its directory does not

A new tag group `swarm` (`none` by default, `required`) is declared on the individual test, for example `test("…", { tags: ["swarm:required"] }, …)`. The `services/api/` directory lock is removed. A browser journey or command check that declares `swarm:required` fails preflight (`SWARM_INSTANCE_UNSUPPORTED`), because those bring their own stack. `pnpm test:run --category ut --swarm required` runs just the declaring tests.

## One generic startup and one queue

The UT layer no longer wraps the shared runner (`.ci/test-catalog.mjs`), and the CI contract now rejects any layer that wraps it. Instead the shared runner (`test/support/tagged/swarm.mjs`) starts one instance and one adapter through the same `scripts/with-jiuwenswarm.sh`, whose command hands its exports back and holds the instance until the run releases it; the wrapper then stops what it started.

- The instance starts only when the frozen plan holds a declaring test, and it starts beside the other groups rather than ahead of them. Only a declaring group waits for it; a run without declaring tests never starts it.
- A file's declaring tests run in a worker process of their own, which holds the instance lock. Declaring work therefore runs one test at a time across all files, while the same file's other tests run in the pool without the instance. There is still exactly one adapter per instance.
- Only declaring processes receive `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXECUTOR`, `SCIENCE_AGENT_ADAPTER_URL` and the gateway endpoints. Every other worker and command check has them removed, even if the calling shell exported them, so a test that boots `createApiServer` without declaring stays on the built-in loop.
- Coverage stays one lcov per Node worker process. A file whose declaring tests run apart is two processes, so the declaring one files its coverage as `<file>.jiuwenswarm.lcov` instead of overwriting the other's (`coverageName` in `test/support/tagged/coordinator.mjs`).
- If the instance cannot start, the declaring tests fail with `SWARM_UNAVAILABLE` and the wrapper's log; everything else still runs. `ut/tagged/timing.json` records the number of declaring tests and how long the instance took to become ready, and `ut/tagged/swarm.log` holds its startup log.

## Which tests declare it

The issue's count (112 / 2 / 5 / 105) came from an earlier tree, so it was re-measured on 9191d552: every Node file in the UT plan was run with the Swarm environment pointed at a recording stand-in adapter, and each request was attributed to the test that sent it (the stand-in's request count matched the attributed count, so no request went unattributed). Only two files send `POST /agent/runs`, which starts a gateway turn, and every planned test that sends it now declares `swarm:required` (29 tests):

- `services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts`, all 9 planned tests: cancelling a queued run; a blocked run holds its Session queue; GET session usage reports gateway token usage; cancelling a blocked run preserves reported model usage; stopping a stuck run; Reviewer stop has its own route; a stuck Session does not block another Session; cancelling a blocked run persists the approval's terminal state; run child stream endpoint serves empty streams.
- `services/api/src/server.test.ts`, 20 of its 78 planned tests: creating a Project opens an implicit Session and refines its title; every later unnamed Session reuses first-message naming; title refinement completes while the first task is running; title refinement persists after the run stream closes; concurrent first messages auto-name only once; an asynchronous title refinement never overwrites a manual rename; a second message never triggers another naming request; an explicitly named Session is never auto-renamed; timeout settings drive live runs; native MCP literature flow; workbench search and Composer references; running sessions accept queued runs; completed runs persist the assistant message identity; an active run keeps its settings snapshot; an Agent-created Skill stays in draft until review; legacy Reviewer does not inject findings; API runs a configured OpenAI-compatible model through the gateway; task `timeout_seconds` is a hard budget; switching to always-allow during a run; switching to ask during a run.

34 other planned `server.test.ts` tests and five other API files (`dashboard`, `mcp/source-api`, `model-usage-api`, `npu-selection-api`, `ssh-host-api`) only pushed web settings to the adapter at server start, which is not a turn; they no longer see the instance. `status:unreviewed` cases stay outside the plan, unchanged.

## One worker count, sized for the public runner

GitHub's runner reference lists a public-repository `ubuntu-latest` runner as 4 CPUs, 16 GB RAM and 14 GB SSD. `UT_WORKERS = 4` in `test/support/tagged/scheduler.mjs` is now the single default for a local `pnpm ci:ut` and the GitHub Actions UT job alike; it does not depend on the host's CPU count. `CI_UT_WORKERS` can only narrow it (`1` for serial diagnosis); a larger value is rejected. No workflow sets a value of its own, and a CI contract test now fails if one does. In `.github/workflows/ci.yml` only a comment changed; the UT job's steps, `timeout-minutes: 60` and coverage arguments are untouched.

Four is the widest the runner sustains. It equals the vCPU count, and memory is far from the limit: under a local cgroup limited to 4 CPUs, 16 GB and no swap, the full UT layer with coverage peaked at 3.2 GB of cgroup memory, page cache included (2.2 GB anonymous), with no OOM kill. More workers would not shorten the run either. With four, the undeclared groups and the serial JiuwenSwarm lane (instance start, then about 330 s of declaring tests on GitHub's runner) finish at about the same time, so the lane, not the pool width, now bounds the UT wall clock.

## Scheduler tests

`test/support/tagged/tests/integration.test.mjs` runs one file's declaring and undeclared tests as two processes and checks that both leave coverage. `test/support/tagged/tests/scheduler.test.mjs` now shows undeclared groups overlapping up to the shared worker count, declaring groups never overlapping (including across files), a file's undeclared tests running beside its declaring lane, the worker-count contract (default 4, 1–4 accepted, 5 or `14` rejected), the environment stripping, and the startup protocol with a stand-in wrapper: the instance's variables are handed over, the wrapper's cleanup runs when the run releases it, and a wrapper that gives up fails the declaring work with its log.

## Validation

On 2428c9ab.

GitHub Actions, this pull request's run on the public `ubuntu-latest` runner (merge with current `main`): every job passed, including Coverage and `merge-gate`.

- UT: PASS, planned 4401, executed 4401, passed 4401, failed 0, skipped 0. Worker pool 4 of 4 CPUs and 15.6 GiB, peak 4. 29 tests declared the instance; it was ready after 40 s, and the two declaring groups took 64 s and 262 s. The test pool took 377 s; in `main`'s last run (9191d552, two workers, the API directory lock) it took 539 s for 4390 tests. The "Run UT" step took 8 min 14 s, against 11 min 15 s, 11 min 28 s and 8 min 26 s in the last three successful `main` runs.
- Coverage: 388 Node lcov files for 388 Node worker processes, 537 source files (536 on `main`), 85 Python source files.
- Mocked E2E (`merge-gate`): planned 99, executed 99, passed 99.

Locally, with the layers run one after another:

- `pnpm ci:ut -- --profile pr --coverage` inside a 4-CPU / 16 GB / no-swap cgroup: PASS, planned 4391, executed 4391, passed 4391, failed 0, skipped 0; worker pool 4, peak 4; 385 lcov files for 385 expected; cgroup memory peak 3.2 GB, no OOM kill. The adapter received 29 settings pushes and 40 `POST /agent/runs`, all from the 29 declaring tests; under the old wrapper every API server any UT test booted pushed its settings there.
- `pnpm ci:st -- --coverage`: planned 24, executed 24, passed 19, failed 5. All five are `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/process-adapters.st.test.ts` ("Runtime exited before completion", and `Error` where `TimeoutError` is expected), and the same layer on unmodified 9191d552 in a separate worktree fails identically (24 / 24 / 19 / 5, the same five tests). The fixture runtime is a `#!/usr/bin/env node` script started with `PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`, and that host has no `node` there; ST passes on GitHub's runner above.
- `pnpm ci:e2e` (all three fixtures, JiuwenSwarm backend): planned 96, executed 96, passed 95, failed 1, skipped 0; the nine JiuwenSwarm checks after the journeys passed. The failure, `test/journey-model-connect-wizard.spec.ts:60` (the model connection success, failure and configuration-protection flow), finds the dialog's submit button ending at 601 px against a 580 px footer; run alone on unmodified 9191d552 it fails with the same values, and it passes on GitHub's runner above. This change touches no web code.
- `pnpm test:run --category ut --swarm required`: planned 29, executed 29, passed 29.
- The first CI run of this pull request failed only its Coverage job: the declaring and undeclared halves of `server.test.ts` wrote the same lcov file, so 387 of 388 expected files arrived. The per-process `coverageName` above fixes it, and the integration test covers it.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable to product behaviour: this changes only how the test runner schedules unit tests and which test processes see the JiuwenSwarm environment. No product code path, API, CLI or UI changed. The mocked browser layer was still run on this commit as a regression check (above).

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none; unit tests run in parallel and the UT job is shorter.
Compatibility and migration: a unit test that needs a real JiuwenSwarm must now declare `swarm:required`; without it, the test runs on the built-in loop. `CI_UT_WORKERS` above 4 is rejected.

450.title: perf(ci): run unit tests in parallel and queue only tests that declare JiuwenSwarm

453.author: zhaozhaozz
453.body:
Fixes #451.

Registering a new shared MCP generation no longer opens a management WebSocket and rewrites config.yaml for every tool. The adapter sends the complete approval map in one request; retiring an inactive generation deletes its permission map in one request as well.

## Behavior and compatibility

- Extend the existing permissions.tools.update and permissions.tools.delete management methods with incremental batch forms. The versioned Swarm patch validates the whole batch before one locked YAML transaction, preserving unrelated tools and rules. Single-tool requests remain compatible.
- Preserve every allow/ask/deny level and the existing policy-conflict rejection. Publish a generation only after permission persistence is acknowledged.
- Preserve the connected server for unchanged catalogs. Active parent generations remain connected until their last run releases them. Failed permission cleanup is retained for retry, including lost acknowledgements during startup.
- Keep the MCP handshake, live probe, session creation, interaction startup, runtime preparation, and their existing logs unchanged. Source installations apply the patch through the existing JiuwenSwarm setup procedure; packaged installations ship it with the adapter.

## Before and after: original J3

Both runs used the unchanged named-environment journey: a new project and session, one shell beat and one closing text. Managed Python was confirmed ready first. All seven steps passed, including the shell output and immutable environment-revision provenance.

| Measurement | Baseline efe07d66 | Candidate fe5fb992 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Tools | 44 | 44 |
| Permission preparation, existing elapsed_ms | 9,383 ms | 607 ms |
| run.started to MCP transport open | 9,547 ms | 789 ms |
| MCP handshake | 6 ms | 12 ms |
| MCP ready to first model-client request preparation | 693 ms | 1,883 ms |
| run.started to completed release | 13.66 s | 8.93 s |
| Whole J3 test | 27.3 s | 53.6 s |
| Named-environment creation step | 7.5 s | 24.6 s |

Permission preparation fell by 8.776 seconds (93.5%) in this pair of runs. Other environment and UI phases varied substantially; these samples support the permission-startup reduction. The model-client log marks preparation before HTTP dispatch.

![Original J3 completed shell output on the tested commit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ccbf2d9-a89d-4527-9302-a10695a3bfd2)

## Swarm session initialization is retained

The historical second 16–18-second gap did not reproduce on the current baseline: session creation totaled 608.3 ms and runtime config totaled 22.4 ms. A new session still needs its own model, tools, rails, and interaction state; existing sessions already reuse their adapter. This PR makes no preparation-cache change.

The same candidate J3 run emitted the existing log lines below, including the approval continuation:

```text
[AgentServer] session adapter created: session_id=8b4644fe-8a04-4ae2-9574-7d8d23540f4b create_instance_ms=1614.6 start_interaction_ms=152.1 total_ms=1770.6
[AgentServer] runtime config applied: session_id=8b4644fe-8a04-4ae2-9574-7d8d23540f4b mode=agent.work.normal total_ms=55.8 cwd_seed=3.8 rail_setters=2.3 eternal_conversation=0.1 runtime_state=0.1 rails_for_mode=41.6 user_interaction=0.0 tools_for_mode=0.1 session_tools=5.5 acp_tools=2.3 prompt_for_mode=0.0 memory_tools=0.0
[AgentServer] runtime config applied: session_id=8b4644fe-8a04-4ae2-9574-7d8d23540f4b mode=agent.work.normal total_ms=21.0 cwd_seed=3.6 rail_setters=2.0 eternal_conversation=0.1 runtime_state=0.1 rails_for_mode=7.8 user_interaction=0.0 tools_for_mode=0.1 session_tools=5.1 acp_tools=2.2 prompt_for_mode=0.0 memory_tools=0.0
```

## Validation and E2E outcome

Tested candidate: fe5fb9921b6031b55402522bc6b0becd6482a0b2. Baseline: efe07d66604c4743ef726eaf05042fd5c42e95ea. UT, ST, baseline ST, candidate mocked browser E2E, baseline mocked browser E2E, and L1 were run sequentially.

- pnpm ci:l1: planned=4, executed=4, passed=4, failed=0, skipped=0.
- Targeted adapter approval/gateway/MCP regressions: 93 passed.
- Batch permission persistence regressions: 5 passed. They exercise the actual management dispatcher and YAML writer, including all levels, one write for 44 tools, one retirement write, invalid-batch atomicity, legacy single-tool compatibility, and concurrent updates.
- pnpm ci:ut: planned=4403, executed=4403, passed=4403, failed=0, skipped=0.
- pnpm ci:st: planned=24, executed=24, passed=18, failed=6, skipped=0. Unmodified efe07d66 produced the identical six failures and identical counts; there are no candidate-only ST failures. The embedded Swarm SDK contract suite passed 79 tests and 20 subtests.
- Mocked browser E2E: planned=99, executed=99, passed=98, failed=1, skipped=0. All nine supplemental Swarm checks passed. The sole browser failure is the existing model-connect wizard layout assertion: the assertion requires submit-button bottom < footer top; observed values are 601.234375 px and 580 px respectively. The unchanged efe07d66 full layer reproduced the same case, line, and values. Baseline E2E: planned=99, executed=99, passed=97, failed=2, skipped=0; no candidate-only failures. Its additional LR-13 failure was a 180-second timeout waiting for its session navigation button; the candidate passed that case, without a causal claim about that difference. Both full layers used E2E_SCIENTIFIC_ENVS=1, one worker, zero retries, and identical 99-case identities.
- Original J3 local-stack/browser journey: PASS, 1 journey / 7 user steps; actual computation succeeded and its environment revision matched. Invocation: npm --prefix .e2e run test:mocked -- journey-prepare-environment.spec.ts --grep 'J3 ' against an isolated stack with scientific environments ready.

Both full E2E logs also emit the existing FRESH_JOURNEY_MUST_RUN_FIRST reporter error for the compact-process fresh-library case. Playwright continues running the planned cases; the counts above do not imply that this ordering contract passed. This PR does not change collection or scheduling.

The five specialist process-adapter ST failures occur when fixture transports exit before protocol completion. Their fixed standard PATH cannot resolve this host's nvm-provided Node. The Evolve distribution ST returns an installation error before reaching its controlled sparse-allocation hook, then fails the evidence assertion; its earlier installation error remains unclassified. Both failure sets reproduce on the untouched baseline. Their assertions and timeouts are unchanged.

## Additional startup observations

These remain report-only:

- Starting J3 while environments are disabled or installing wastes a startup/test window, typically tens of seconds. A readiness preflight preserves the existing environment, computation, and provenance assertions.
- Swarm waits a fixed six seconds after gateway readiness. An actual agent-server readiness check could save up to six seconds per stack while preserving the readiness guarantee.
- Setup and start both apply the same configuration, even when its text is unchanged. Direct savings are likely milliseconds and below one second per stack; invalidation overhead has not been isolated.
- Default-route probes can return 503 before a default model is configured. Avoiding only those unusable probes may save milliseconds to seconds per startup, depending on retry backoff; valid-model capability checks must remain.

Gateway 400 handling, environment cloning, reviewer quiet windows, journey length, worker counts, slowMo, and UT scheduling are unchanged.

## Release

Release category: release:performance
User impact: shorter startup when a run introduces a new tool catalog, with the same tool permissions and outcomes.
Compatibility and migration: no application-data migration; deploy the adapter with the versioned Swarm patch through the existing setup/build path.
